title: How Search Engines Decide Which Pages Rank First

content: When you type a question into a search engine, it does not search the live internet. It searches a huge index built in advance by automated programs called crawlers, which follow links from page to page and store what they find.

Ranking then works by scoring indexed pages against your query. Search companies say they weigh signals such as how well a page matches the words and meaning of the query, the quality and usefulness of the content, how trustworthy the site appears, and how easy the page is to use on a phone.

No one outside the search companies knows the exact formulas, and they change often. For publishers, the safest approach is plain: write original, accurate pages, make them fast, and make clear who wrote them.
author: BubblesEdiy News Desk
